questions.question: What does the voltage of a battery measure in an electric circuit?
options: The total number of electrons present in the wires
The rate at which energy is lost as heat in the resistors
The strength with which it can 'push' current around the circuit
The physical size and length of the connecting wires

questions.question: In a series circuit, how does the voltage across each component relate to the total voltage of the battery?
options: The voltage across each component is always equal to the battery's voltage
The voltages across each component add up to the total voltage of the cell or battery
The voltage across each component is subtracted from the battery's voltage to find the current
The voltage across each component is completely independent of the battery's voltage

questions.question: If three 1.5V cells are connected in series to form a battery, what is the total voltage of this battery?
In which direction does a battery push electric charge (electrons) around a complete circuit?
options: It pushes them one way round a complete circuit
It pushes them back and forth continuously
It pushes them from both terminals toward the middle simultaneously
It pushes them outwards in all directions into the surrounding air

questions.question: What happens to the electrons in a circuit at the moment it is turned on?
options: Electrons only near the positive terminal begin to move first
Electrons everywhere in the circuit start moving at the same time
Electrons must travel all the way from the battery to the bulb before any light is produced
Electrons in the wires stop moving to allow the current to pass

questions.question: At what speed do individual electrons typically move around an electric circuit?
options: At the speed of light
A few kilometres per hour
A speed of just a few millimetres each second
They do not move at all

questions.question: Why does a faulty filament bulb prevent electric current from flowing through it?
options: The glass bulb has become too hot to conduct electricity
The metal base has changed into an insulator
The filament inside the bulb is broken
The bulb is trying to push current in the opposite direction

questions.question: If a series circuit has one faulty component, how can you make the rest of the circuit work?
options: By adding another battery in the opposite direction
By using a wire to bypass the faulty component
By replacing all the working components with larger ones
By cutting the circuit wires shorter

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a series circuit?
options: A circuit with multiple branching pathways for the current
An electric circuit with one complete loop from one end of a battery to the other
A circuit that only functions when static electricity is present
A circuit where components are connected to different power sources

questions.question: What effect does an ammeter have on the current in the circuit it is connected into?
options: It significantly reduces the current to protect the components
It doubles the current to make it easier to read
It measures the current flowing through it without affecting the current in the circuit
It stops the current completely while taking a measurement

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the current in a series circuit is true?
options: The current is strongest near the positive terminal of the battery
The current in a series circuit is the same everywhere
The current decreases after passing through each bulb
The current is weakest near the negative terminal of the battery

questions.question: What happens to the current in a series circuit when you add another component to it?
options: The current only decreases on the side after the new component
The current only decreases on the side before the new component
It changes the current everywhere, on both sides of the component
The current remains exactly the same everywhere

questions.question: How should a voltmeter be connected to measure the voltage across a component?
options: In series, as part of the main loop of the circuit
It is connected across the terminals of the component
Inside the battery compartment itself
Connected to only one end of the component with a single wire

questions.question: How do two objects with opposite electric charges behave when they are brought near each other?
options: They attract each other
They repel each other
They cancel each other's charge without moving
They do not exert any force on each other

questions.question: Why is it difficult to build up a static charge on metal objects by rubbing them?
options: Metals do not contain any electrons
Electric charge flows through them, preventing charge from building up
Friction cannot transfer electrons to metal surfaces
Metals immediately destroy any electric charge they touch
